species.name: Sprigatito
species.flavor: The sweet scent its body gives off mesmerizes those around it. The scent grows stronger when this Pokémon is in the sun.

species.name: Floragato
species.flavor: The hardness of Floragato’s fur depends on the Pokémon’s mood. When Floragato is prepared to battle, its fur becomes pointed and needle sharp.

species.name: Meowscarada
species.flavor: With skillful misdirection, it rigs foes with pollen-packed flower bombs. Meowscarada sets off the bombs before its foes realize what’s going on.

species.name: Fuecoco
species.flavor: Its flame sac is small, so energy is always leaking out. This energy is released from the dent atop Fuecoco’s head and flickers to and fro.

species.name: Crocalor
species.flavor: The valve in Crocalor’s flame sac is closely connected to its vocal cords. This Pokémon utters a guttural cry as it spews flames every which way.

species.name: Skeledirge
species.flavor: Skeledirge’s gentle singing soothes the souls of all that hear it. It burns its enemies to a crisp with flames of over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit.

species.name: Quaxly
species.flavor: Its strong legs let it easily swim around in even fast-flowing rivers. It likes to keep things tidy and is prone to overthinking things.

species.name: Quaxwell
species.flavor: The hardworking Quaxwell observes people and Pokémon from various regions and incorporates their movements into its own dance routines.

species.name: Quaquaval
species.flavor: Dancing in ways that evoke far-away places, this Pokémon mesmerizes all that see it. Flourishes of its decorative water feathers slice into its foes.

species.name: Lechonk
species.flavor: This Pokémon spurns all but the finest of foods. Its body gives off an herblike scent that bug Pokémon detest.

species.name: Oinkologne
species.flavor: It entrances female Pokémon with the sweet, alluring scent that wafts from all over its body.

species.name: Tarountula
species.flavor: The thread it secretes from its rear is as strong as wire. The secret behind the thread’s strength is the topic of ongoing research.

species.name: Spidops
species.flavor: Spidops covers its territory in tough, sticky threads to set up traps for intruders.

species.name: Nymble
species.flavor: It’s highly skilled at a fighting style in which it uses its jumping capabilities to dodge incoming attacks while also dealing damage to opponents.

species.name: Lokix
species.flavor: It uses its normally folded third set of legs when in Showdown Mode. This places a huge burden on its body, so it can’t stay in this mode for long.

species.name: Pawmi
species.flavor: The pads of its paws are electricity-discharging organs. Pawmi fires electricity from its forepaws while standing unsteadily on its hind legs.

species.name: Pawmo
species.flavor: Pawmo uses a unique fighting technique in which it uses its forepaws to strike foes and zap them with electricity from its paw pads simultaneously.

species.name: Pawmot
species.flavor: Pawmot’s fluffy fur acts as a battery. It can store the same amount of electricity as an electric car.

species.name: Tandemaus
species.flavor: The pair sticks together no matter what. They split any food they find exactly in half and then eat it together.

species.name: Maushold
species.flavor: The larger pair protects the little ones during battles. When facing strong opponents, the whole group will join the fight.

species.name: Fidough
species.flavor: The yeast in Fidough’s breath is useful for cooking, so this Pokémon has been protected by people since long ago.

species.name: Dachsbun
species.flavor: The surface of this Pokémon’s skin hardens when exposed to intense heat, and its body has an appetizing aroma.

species.name: Smoliv
species.flavor: This Pokémon converts nutrients into oil, which it stores in the fruit on its head. It can easily go a whole week without eating or drinking.

species.name: Dolliv
species.flavor: It basks in the sun to its heart’s content until the fruits on its head ripen. After that, Dolliv departs from human settlements and goes on a journey.

species.name: Arboliva
species.flavor: This Pokémon drives back enemies by launching its rich, aromatic oil at them with enough force to smash a boulder.

species.name: Squawkabilly
species.flavor: Green-feathered flocks hold the most sway. When they’re out searching for food in the mornings and evenings, it gets very noisy.

species.name: Nacli
species.flavor: The ground scrapes its body as it travels, causing it to leave salt behind. Salt is constantly being created and replenished inside Nacli’s body.

species.name: Naclstack
species.flavor: It compresses rock salt inside its body and shoots out hardened salt pellets with enough force to perforate an iron sheet.

species.name: Garganacl
species.flavor: Many Pokémon gather around Garganacl, hoping to lick at its mineral-rich salt.

species.name: Charcadet
species.flavor: Its firepower increases when it fights, reaching over 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit. It likes berries that are rich in fat.

species.name: Armarouge
species.flavor: This Pokémon clads itself in armor that has been fortified by psychic and fire energy, and it shoots blazing fireballs.

species.name: Ceruledge
species.flavor: An old set of armor steeped in grudges caused this Pokémon’s evolution. Ceruledge cuts its enemies to pieces without mercy.

species.name: Tadbulb
species.flavor: It floats using the electricity stored in its body. When thunderclouds are around, Tadbulb will float higher off the ground.

species.name: Bellibolt
species.flavor: What appear to be eyeballs are actually organs for discharging the electricity generated by Bellibolt’s belly-button dynamo.

species.name: Wattrel
species.flavor: These Pokémon make their nests on coastal cliffs. The nests have a strange, crackling texture, and they’re a popular delicacy.

species.name: Kilowattrel
species.flavor: It uses its throat sac to store electricity generated by its wings. There’s hardly any oil in its feathers, so it is a poor swimmer.

species.name: Maschiff
species.flavor: Its well-developed jaw and fangs are strong enough to crunch through boulders, and its thick fat makes for an excellent defense.

species.name: Mabosstiff
species.flavor: Mabosstiff loves playing with children. Though usually gentle, it takes on an intimidating look when protecting its family.

species.name: Shroodle
species.flavor: To keep enemies away from its territory, it paints markings around its nest using a poisonous liquid that has an acrid odor.

species.name: Grafaiai
species.flavor: Each Grafaiai paints its own individual pattern, and it will paint that same pattern over and over again throughout its life.

species.name: Bramblin
species.flavor: Not even Bramblin knows where it is headed as it tumbles across the wilderness, blown by the wind. It loathes getting wet.

species.name: Brambleghast
species.flavor: Brambleghast wanders around arid regions. On rare occasions, mass outbreaks of these Pokémon will bury an entire town.

species.name: Toedscool
species.flavor: Though it looks like Tentacool, Toedscool is a completely different species. Its legs may be thin, but it can run at a speed of 30 mph.

species.name: Toedscruel
species.flavor: It coils its 10 tentacles around prey and sucks out their nutrients, causing the prey pain. The folds along the rim of its head are a popular delicacy.

species.name: Klawf
species.flavor: This Pokémon lives on sheer cliffs. It sidesteps opponents’ attacks, then lunges for their weak spots with its claws.

species.name: Capsakid
species.flavor: Traditional Paldean dishes can be extremely spicy because they include the shed front teeth of Capsakid among their ingredients.

species.name: Scovillain
species.flavor: The green head has turned vicious due to the spicy chemicals stimulating its brain. Once it goes on a rampage, there is no stopping it.

species.name: Rellor
species.flavor: It rolls its mud ball around while the energy it needs for evolution matures. Eventually the time comes for it to evolve.

species.name: Rabsca
species.flavor: An infant sleeps inside the ball. Rabsca rolls the ball soothingly with its legs to ensure the infant sleeps comfortably.

species.name: Flittle
species.flavor: It spends its time running around wastelands. If anyone steals its beloved berries, it will chase them down and exact its revenge.

species.name: Espathra
species.flavor: It emits psychic power from the gaps between its multicolored frills and sprints at speeds greater than 120 mph.

species.name: Tinkatink
species.flavor: This Pokémon pounds iron scraps together to make a hammer. It will remake the hammer again and again until it’s satisfied with the result.

species.name: Tinkatuff
species.flavor: These Pokémon make their homes in piles of scrap metal. They test the strength of each other’s hammers by smashing them together.

species.name: Tinkaton
species.flavor: The hammer tops 220 pounds, yet it gets swung around easily by Tinkaton as it steals whatever it pleases and carries its plunder back home.

species.name: Wiglett
species.flavor: Though it looks like Diglett, Wiglett is an entirely different species. The resemblance seems to be a coincidental result of environmental adaptation.

species.name: Wugtrio
species.flavor: A variety of fish Pokémon, Wugtrio was once considered to be a regional form of Dugtrio.

species.name: Bombirdier
species.flavor: Bombirdier uses the apron on its chest to bundle up food, which it carries back to its nest. It enjoys dropping things that make loud noises.

species.name: Finizen
species.flavor: Its water ring is made from seawater mixed with a sticky fluid that Finizen secretes from its blowhole.

species.name: Palafin
species.flavor: Its physical capabilities are no different than a Finizen’s, but when its allies are in danger, it transforms and powers itself up.

species.name: Varoom
species.flavor: The steel section is Varoom’s actual body. This Pokémon clings to rocks and converts the minerals within into energy to fuel its activities.

species.name: Revavroom
species.flavor: Revavroom viciously threatens others with the sound of its exhaust. It sticks its tongue out from its cylindrical mouth and sprays toxic fluids.

species.name: Cyclizar
species.flavor: It can sprint at over 70 mph while carrying a human. The rider’s body heat warms Cyclizar’s back and lifts the Pokémon’s spirit.

species.name: Orthworm
species.flavor: This Pokémon lives in arid deserts. It maintains its metal body by consuming iron from the soil.

species.name: Glimmet
species.flavor: Glimmet’s toxic mineral crystals look just like flower petals. This Pokémon scatters poisonous powder like pollen to protect itself.

species.name: Glimmora
species.flavor: Glimmora’s petals are made of crystallized poison energy. It has recently become evident that these petals resemble Tera Jewels.

species.name: Greavard
species.flavor: This friendly Pokémon doesn’t like being alone. Pay it even the slightest bit of attention, and it will follow you forever.

species.name: Houndstone
species.flavor: A lovingly mourned Pokémon was reborn as Houndstone. It doesn’t like anyone touching the protuberance atop its head.

species.name: Flamigo
species.flavor: Thanks to a behavior of theirs known as “synchronizing,” an entire flock of these Pokémon can attack simultaneously in perfect harmony.

species.name: Cetoddle
species.flavor: It lives in frigid regions in pods of five or so individuals. It loves the minerals found in snow and ice.

species.name: Cetitan
species.flavor: Ice energy builds up in the horn on its upper jaw, causing the horn to reach cryogenic temperatures that freeze its surroundings.

species.name: Veluza
species.flavor: Veluza has excellent regenerative capabilities. It sheds spare flesh from its body to boost its agility, then charges at its prey.

species.name: Dondozo
species.flavor: It treats Tatsugiri like its boss and follows it loyally. Though powerful, Dondozo is apparently not very smart.

species.name: Tatsugiri
species.flavor: Tatsugiri is an extremely cunning Pokémon. It feigns weakness to lure in prey, then orders its partner to attack.

species.name: Annihilape
species.flavor: It imbues its fists with the power of the rage that it kept hidden in its heart. Opponents struck by these imbued fists will be shattered to their core.

species.name: Clodsire
species.flavor: It lives at the bottom of ponds and swamps. It will carry Wooper on its back and ferry them across water from one shore to the other.

species.name: Farigiraf
species.flavor: The hardened head from the tail protects the head of the main body as Farigiraf whips its long neck around to headbutt enemies.

species.name: Dudunsparce
species.flavor: It drives enemies out of its nest by sucking in enough air to fill its long, narrow lungs, then releasing the air in an intense blast.

species.name: Kingambit
species.flavor: Though it commands a massive army in battle, it’s not skilled at devising complex strategies. It just uses brute strength to keep pushing.

species.name: Great Tusk
species.flavor: This creature resembles a mysterious Pokémon that, according to a paranormal magazine, has lived since ancient times.

species.name: Scream Tail
species.flavor: It resembles a mysterious Pokémon described in a paranormal magazine as a Jigglypuff from one billion years ago.

species.name: Brute Bonnet
species.flavor: It bears a slight resemblance to a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a cross between a dinosaur and a mushroom.

species.name: Flutter Mane
species.flavor: It has similar features to a ghostly pterosaur that was covered in a paranormal magazine, but the two have little else in common.

species.name: Slither Wing
species.flavor: This Pokémon somewhat resembles an ancient form of Volcarona that was introduced in a dubious magazine.

species.name: Sandy Shocks
species.flavor: No records exist of this Pokémon being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with a creature shown in an expedition journal.

species.name: Iron Treads
species.flavor: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. It resembles a mysterious object described in an old expedition journal.

species.name: Iron Bundle
species.flavor: It resembles a mysterious object mentioned in an old book. There are only two reported sightings of this Pokémon.

species.name: Iron Hands
species.flavor: This Pokémon shares many similarities with Iron Hands, an object mentioned in a certain expedition journal.

species.name: Iron Jugulis
species.flavor: It’s possible that Iron Jugulis, an object described in an old book, may actually be this Pokémon.

species.name: Iron Moth
species.flavor: No records exist of this species being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with an object described in an old book.

species.name: Iron Thorns
species.flavor: Some of its notable features match those of an object named within a certain expedition journal as Iron Thorns.

species.name: Frigibax
species.flavor: This Pokémon lives in forests and craggy areas. Using the power of its dorsal fin, it cools the inside of its nest like a refrigerator.

species.name: Arctibax
species.flavor: It attacks with the blade of its frozen dorsal fin by doing a front flip in the air. Arctibax’s strong back and legs allow it to pull off this technique.

species.name: Baxcalibur
species.flavor: It launches itself into battle by flipping upside down and spewing frigid air from its mouth. It finishes opponents off with its dorsal blade.

species.name: Gimmighoul
species.flavor: It lives inside an old treasure chest. Sometimes it gets left in shop corners since no one realizes it’s actually a Pokémon.

species.name: Gholdengo
species.flavor: It has a sturdy body made up of stacked coins. Gholdengo overwhelms its enemies by firing coin after coin at them in quick succession.

species.name: Wo-Chien
species.flavor: It drains the life-force from vegetation, causing nearby forests to instantly wither and fields to turn barren.

species.name: Chien-Pao
species.flavor: The hatred of those who perished by the sword long ago has clad itself in snow and become a Pokémon.

species.name: Ting-Lu
species.flavor: It slowly brings its exceedingly heavy head down upon the ground, splitting the earth open with huge fissures that run over 160 feet deep.

species.name: Chi-Yu
species.flavor: The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon.

species.name: Roaring Moon
species.flavor: According to an article in a dubious magazine, this Pokémon has some connection to a phenomenon that occurs in a certain region.

species.name: Iron Valiant
species.flavor: It’s possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.

species.name: Koraidon
species.flavor: This Pokémon resembles Cyclizar, but it is far burlier and more ferocious. Nothing is known about its ecology or other features.

species.name: Miraidon
species.flavor: This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning.

species.name: Walking Wake
species.flavor: It resembles an illustration published in a paranormal magazine, said to be a depiction of a super-ancient Suicune.

species.name: Iron Leaves
species.flavor: According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders.

species.name: Dipplin
species.flavor: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.

species.name: Poltchageist
species.flavor: Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated.

species.name: Sinistcha
species.flavor: It prefers cool, dark places, such as the back of a shelf or the space beneath a home's floorboards. It wanders in search of prey after sunset.

species.name: Okidogi
species.flavor: Okidogi is a ruffian with a short temper. It can pulverize anything by swinging around the chain on its neck.

species.name: Munkidori
species.flavor: Munkidori keeps itself somewhere safe while it toys with its foes, using psychokinesis to induce intense dizziness.

species.name: Fezandipiti
species.flavor: Fezandipiti beats its glossy wings to scatter pheromones that captivate people and Pokémon.

species.name: Ogerpon
species.flavor: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.

species.name: Archaludon
species.flavor: It digs holes on mountains, searching for food. It’s so durable that being caught in a cave-in won’t faze it.

species.name: Hydrapple
species.flavor: These capricious syrpents have banded together. On the rare occasion that their moods align, their true power is unleashed.

species.name: Gouging Fire
species.flavor: It resembles an eerie Pokémon once shown in a paranormal magazine. That Pokémon was said to be an Entei regenerated from a fossil.

species.name: Raging Bolt
species.flavor: It bears resemblance to a Pokémon that became a hot topic for a short while after a paranormal magazine touted it as Raikou's ancestor.

species.name: Iron Boulder
species.flavor: It was named after a mysterious object recorded in an old book. Its body seems to be metallic.

species.name: Iron Crown
species.flavor: There was supposedly an incident in which it launched shining blades to cut everything around it to pieces. Little else is known about it.

species.name: Terapagos
species.flavor: It’s thought that this Pokémon lived in ancient Paldea until it got caught in seismic shifts and went extinct.

species.name: Pecharunt
species.flavor: Its peach-shaped shell serves as storage for a potent poison. It makes poisonous mochi and serves them to people and Pokémon.
